1  -2-  WP No. 44579 of 2018  THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR DICTATING ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Challenging order dated 31.08.2018 passed on I.A.no.IX filed under Order VI Rule 17 CPC passed by Senior Civil Judge, Maddur, in MVC No.1512/2015 and consequently allowed IA no.IX, this writ petition is filed.
2.

Sri N.S. Bhat, learned counsel for petitioner submitted that on 08.05.2014 at about 1:30 p.m., Sri.
Shivanna dashed his motorcycle bearing registration no. KA-1-V-5776 against a dog crossing road near Shivalli Vyshali restaurant near Bilikere gate on Mysuru-Bengaluru Road.

Due to said accident,
petitioner, who was pillion rider as well as Shivanna - rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
It was stated that respondent no.1 - owner of motorcycle and respondent no.2 - insurer.

It was further submitted that claiming compensation for injuries sustained, petitioner filed MVC no.1512/2015 against owner and insurer under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act ('M.V. Act' for brevity).
3.
On entering appearance, respondents filed written statement denying accident and claim.
Thereafter tribunal recorded evidence of claimant as PW.1 on 17.03.2016 and marked Exs.P1 to P7.
Thereafter on 13.07.2016, respondent - no.2 - insurer filed application for permission to file written statement was allowed.
Issues were framed on 31.08.2016, and on 27.09.2016, claimant examined himself further and marked Exs.P.8 to P.16.

On 28.02.2017 doctor was examined as PW.2 and Exs.
P.17 to P.20 were marked.

4. Subsequently on 21.03.2018 - owner filed application for permission to file written statement,
which was allowed.

In view of specific explanation regarding events that occurred immediately after accident being pleaded, petitioner (claimant) filed I.A.no.IX under Order VI Rule 17 of CPC for amendment of claim petition to add two paragraphs.
A memo was also filed on 08.08.2018 producing supporting documents.
Under impugned order, tribunal rejected said application for amendment with cost of Rs.500/-.
Aggrieved thereby, this writ petition is filed.
5. It was submitted that Division Bench of this Court in Salamma Vs. K.V. Ramachandra1, held that in a claim ILR 1973 Mysore 339 petition under MV Act, strict rules of evidence do not apply.

Learned counsel for petitioner further relied upon decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sampath Kumar vs. Ayyakannu and Anr.2, and in Varun Pahwa vs. Mrs. Renu Chaudhary3, and decision of High Court of Punjab and Haryana in case of Raj Mohinder Singh vs. Surinder Kaur alias Surinder and Ors.4, to contend that approach of Court towards application for amendment would have to be liberal and amendments to bring out real controversy should not be rejected.

6. On other hand, learned counsel for respondent - insurer submitted that amendment sought was four years after filing of claim petition.
It was further submitted that trial had commenced, wherein claimant had examined himself and also PW-2 - doctor and got marked Exhibits P1 to P20.
At stage of cross-examination of PW.2 - doctor, application for amendment was filed which would be unnecessary and also change basis on which claim petition was filed.

It was submitted that claimant AIR 2002 SC 3369 AIR 2019 SC 1186 AIR 2019 P&H 32 being one of victims and eyewitness to accident had already deposed about manner of accident and events that occurred thereafter during treatment.

Such being case, there was absolutely no justification for seeking amendment and Tribunal was fully justified in dismissing same.
7.
Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition records.
8. From above submission, question that would arise herein is, about justification for seeking amendment after commencement of trial and rejection of application for amendment.
9. Law regarding amendment of pleadings is governed by Order VI Rule 17 of CPC is fairly well settled.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Rajkumar Gurawara (Dead) Thr. L.Rs vs. M/s.
S.K.Sarwagi and Co. Pvt. Ltd. and Anr

sentences.text: .,5 held that application for amendment should be treated liberally prior to commencement of trial.
But, after commencement of trial, consideration of application has to be light of proviso to Order VI Rule 17 of CPC.
AIR 2008 Supreme Court 2303 10.
In instant case, amendment sought is to insert two paragraphs in Column no.22 of claim petition regarding events that occurred in hospital wherein claimant/injured were admitted for treatment.
In claim petition, it is stated that accident occurred when dog suddenly came across road and rider/pillion rider of motorcycle fell down and sustained injuries.

Amendment now sought is to include explanation about amendment of history of accident as per hospital records was not due to self-fall, but due to accident caused on account of dog suddenly came across road and about time of accident.
Though strict rules of evidence may not apply to claim petitions as nature of enquiry is summary, principles governing amendment and law of evidence would still be applicable.
Rules regarding filing of claim petition would require claimants to produce copies of documents in support of their claim to be filed along with claim petition.
Claimant has in fact got marked wound certificate and MLC Register extract during deposition of PW.2 - doctor.
11. In any circumstances, necessitating correction carried out in hospital records, doctor would be proper person to depose about same.

Admittedly deposition of PW.2 - doctor is not yet completed prior to filing of claim petition, nothing prevented petitioner from pleading same in claim petition than to seek amendment to insert explanation after commencement of trial that too after claimant is fully examined/cross-examined and at stage of cross-examination of PW.2 - doctor.
Same would amount to filling up of lacuna in evidence, which would be contrary to intention and purpose for permitting amendment.

3 12.
While passing impugned order, Tribunal has stated that trial had already commenced wherein claimant was examined and matter was listed for further evidence of claimant's side.

It has specifically stated that respondent had elicited several admissions during cross-examination of claimant as PW.1 and to overcome said admissions, amendment was sought and it would change nature of cause of action.
As said reasoning is in accordance with law, I do not see any justification to interfere with same.
13. Further, Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sampath Kumar's case (supra), was considering an application for amendment of plaint filed before commencement of trial.
It is settled law that amendment prior to commencement of trial have to be considered liberally unlike in present case where application is filed after commencement of trial.

Even in Varun Pahawa's case (supra),
amendment sought was only to rectify an incorrect description of plaintiff in plaint.
Considering nature of amendment sought, Hon'ble Supreme Court held that application should not be rejected on technical interpretation.
In Raj Mohinder Singh's case (supra), High Court of Punjab and Haryana, applied real controversy test.

entities.text: High Court of Punjab and Haryana
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: But in instant case, claimant having pleaded that accident occurred when dog suddenly came across road and rider of motorcycle fell down and sustained injuries.
If history of injuries as recorded in hospital records was corrected by concerned doctor on same day, said fact cannot be stated to be without knowledge of claimant at time of filing claim petition.
Amendment sought after completion of cross-examination would not bring present case within ratio of said case.
14. Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar Gurawara's case (supra) has held in light of proviso to Order VI Rule 17 of CPC that amendment after commencement of trial would be prohibited.
Therefore, there is no merit in writ petition.
Accordingly, writ petition is dismissed.

However, observations and findings of this Court are confined to I.A. filed for amendment and shall not bind tribunal while deciding claim petition.
